subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Obsolescence and Spoilage
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Obsolescence and Spoilage.

hook.text: A tech company writes off $50 million in unsold tablets. The new model launched and nobody wants the old one.

buildup.text: Obsolescence occurs when inventory loses value because of new models, changing trends, or expired shelf life.

discovery.text: Perishable goods spoil. Fashion becomes outdated. Technology gets replaced. Time is the enemy of inventory.

twist.text: Companies often hold obsolete stock for too long hoping it will sell. Denial makes the write-off bigger.

climax.text: Regular inventory reviews that identify slow-movers early allow discounts or donations before total loss.

punchline.text: Inventory has a shelf life—even when it doesn't expire.

quiz.question: Why is obsolete inventory often held too long?
options: Companies hope it will eventually sell
